problem: Image-goal navigation policies trained on navigation-specific data generalize poorly to new environments, and foundation-model text-level reasoning cannot be grasped by low-level policy networks, so the internet-scale logical knowledge is not effectively used for control.
motivation: Navigation datasets cannot cover every household environment, while VLMs and diffusion models carry broad world knowledge. The paper observes that predicting the next visual state gives the policy a concrete, modality-aligned subgoal, decoupling high-level reasoning from low-level control.
key_idea: Use an MLLM (LLaVA) plus an edit-based diffusion model to predict a future observation frame k steps ahead, and feed it with the current and goal images into a hybrid-fusion RL policy that outputs actions.
insight: Visual subgoal prediction lets the policy focus only on the current-to-next-frame relation, and the gains are largest when policy training data is scarce (1/4 and 1/8 Gibson: SR 81.2 vs 77.9 and 71.1 vs 68.1). The fusion ablation shows how the future frame is injected matters enormously: Hybrid Fusion gets 91.0 SR versus 40.1 for Early Fusion and 13.7 for Late Fusion.
method: Data formulation: tuples (x_t, x_{t+k}, x_h, y, x_g) from shortest-path-follower videos in simulation and from human-teleoperated ego-view videos in the real world, with interval k=5.
Predictor MLLM: LLaVA (CLIP ViT-L/14 + Vicuna-7B) fine-tuned with LoRA takes the current observation, goal image and instruction and emits special <image> tokens.

Future Frame Prediction Model: a Q-Former maps the <image> hidden states to f^N; a fusion block (2 self-attention, 1 cross-attention, MLP) merges them with the history-frame feature f^H into f*; f* conditions an InstructPix2Pix-style latent diffusion model (VAE latent, noise-prediction loss) to generate the future frame; the diffusion weights are first pre-trained with IP2P on navigation data.

Hybrid Fusion Policy: one branch concatenates the current observation and the future frame along the RGB channels (trainable 2D encoder, f_p); the other concatenates the current observation and the goal image (pre-trained encoder, f_o); [f_p, f_o, a_{t-1}] feeds a recurrent actor-critic trained end-to-end with PPO.
Test-time loop: the Predictor generates a future frame, the policy executes k steps toward it, then the frame is regenerated, repeating until the step limit T=500 or stop.
Fusion ablation: compares Early Fusion (all three images channel-concatenated), Late Fusion (separate encoders, feature-level fusion) and Hybrid Fusion.

setting.backbone: LLaVA (CLIP ViT-L/14 + Vicuna-7B, LoRA fine-tuned) + Q-Former + latent diffusion (InstructPix2Pix-based) predictor; RL-trained recurrent actor-critic policy with a 2D visual encoder
setting.training_data: Gibson ImageNav training scenes (72 scenes): predictor trained on shortest-path video frames (k=5); policy trained with PPO for 500M steps on full, 1/4 or 1/8 of Gibson data; real-world human-teleoperated videos for real-robot predictor data
setting.observation: monocular RGB 128x128, 90° FOV, plus goal image (and optional text instruction)
setting.action_space: discrete low-level: MOVE_FORWARD 0.25 m, TURN_LEFT 30°, TURN_RIGHT 30°, STOP

results: On Gibson ImageNav, NavigateDiff reaches 91.0% SR / 64.8% SPL with full data, slightly higher SR than FGPrompt (90.4) but lower SPL (66.5). With 1/4 and 1/8 data it beats FGPrompt (SR 81.2 vs 77.9; 71.1 vs 68.1) and transfers better to MP3D (SR 68.0 vs 65.7 at 1/4). It also beats FGPrompt on real-world SR in three indoor scenes.
limitations: Predictor's image quality gains over fine-tuned IP2P are marginal (FID 25.93 vs 26.59), and generating a frame every k steps adds computational cost.
Full-data SPL is below FGPrompt (64.8 vs 66.5); real-world evaluation is small and the parking lot SPL is lower than the baseline.
'Zero-shot' is limited to unseen environments; the predictor and policy are still trained on Gibson data and require task-specific training.
builds_on: SEED/GILL-style MLLM-diffusion (Koh et al. generating images with MLLMs)
